name: Kim Gordon
label: Matador
lede: She picked up a bass at 27 with no experience, co-founded Sonic Youth, and at 70 was ranked No. 10 on Pitchfork's 2024 list with a record built on trap beats.

eras.title: An art student who never planned on a band
eras.text: Gordon grew up in Rochester and Los Angeles and trained as a visual artist. She reached New York in 1980 to make art, wrote for Artforum, and only then drifted into the downtown noise scene.

years.h: Kim Gordon graduates from Otis with a BFA
years.p: Before any guitar, she studied art in Los Angeles, including a short stretch working for the dealer Larry Gagosian.
years.xp: Born in Rochester in 1953, Gordon moved to Los Angeles at five when her father took a professorship at UCLA. She did two years at Santa Monica College, tried York University in Toronto and left homesick, then finished at Otis College of Art and Design.

years.h: She moves to New York to make art, not music
years.p: Gordon wrote for Artforum and started Design Office, a project of interventions in friends' apartments.
years.xp: In 1981 she curated a show at White Columns gallery with work by Mike Kelley and Tony Oursler. The gallery would matter again within months: it hosted the Noise Fest where Sonic Youth first played.

eras.title: Three guitars, no drummer
eras.text: Gordon, 27 and new to every instrument, started with CKM, then formed Sonic Youth with Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo. The band spent four years and three drummers finding its sound in New York's noise scene.

years.h: Kim Gordon joins CKM, her first band, never having played
years.p: Through bandmate Stanton Miranda she met [[Lee Ranaldo|6eb1f3f8-5c5a-41c2-a390-f397a2b824a3]] and [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]], and began dating Moore.

years.cap: Kim Gordon at the Venice Film Festival · Wikimedia
years.h: Sonic Youth plays Noise Fest at White Columns, without a drummer
years.p: The trio of Gordon, Moore and Ranaldo did three songs at the gallery Gordon had curated at that year, where Ranaldo was also playing in [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]]'s guitar ensemble.
years.xp:
The name came together in mid-1981: Fred "Sonic" Smith of the MC5 plus the reggae artist Big Youth. Gordon later said a certain sound arrived the moment Moore came up with it.

Richard Edson drummed first (1981 to 1982), then [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] (1982 to 1985).

years.h: Glenn Branca signs Sonic Youth to Neutral Records
years.p: The label released the self-titled 1982 EP, their first record, to good reviews and almost no distribution.

years.h: Confusion Is Sex · Neutral
years.p: Gordon sings, plays bass and guitar and co-produces the first album. It includes a live Stooges cover, with Bob Bert on drums.
years.xp: Critics split: Entertainment Weekly's Chuck Eddy later called it the band's funniest, hardest-rocking and most underrated album, while the Chicago Tribune's Greg Kot said the noise-guitar revolution fell flat on tape.

years.h: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore marry
years.p: The couple's marriage lasted 27 years and ran through the whole of Sonic Youth.

years.h: Steve Shelley takes the drum stool and stays 26 years
years.p: After Edson and Bert, Shelley completes the lineup of Gordon, Moore, Ranaldo and Shelley that would never change until the end.

eras.title: SST, Sister, and the dream nation
eras.text: A deal with SST in 1986 took the band national. By the end of the decade Gordon had co-written a double album that critics called the year's second best, and was already running side projects.

years.h: Sister · SST
years.p: Recorded on analog gear at Sear Sound in Manhattan over March and April 1987, a loose concept record inspired by the science-fiction writer Philip K. Dick.
years.xp: The opener "Schizophrenia" was originally titled "Sister". Wikipedia reports Gordon's own brother's schizophrenia partly inspired it. Pitchfork later ranked the record 14th on its best albums of the 1980s.

years.cap: Daydream Nation, cover painting by Gerhard Richter.
years.h: Daydream Nation: a double album with a Richter candle on the cover
years.p: Recorded July and August 1988 at Greene St. Recording in Manhattan, with Gordon singing "The Sprawl" and "Kissability".
years.xp: The cover is a 1983 Gerhard Richter painting called Kerze (Candle). NME gave the album a perfect score, Rolling Stone ranked it second of 1988, and the Village Voice's Pazz and Jop poll also put it second. The Library of Congress later chose it for the National Recording Registry.

eras.title: Geffen money, and a side life
eras.text: Sonic Youth went major with Goo, toured with Nirvana, and headlined Lollapalooza. Gordon meanwhile produced Hole, started Free Kitten, launched a clothing line and raised a daughter.

years.h: Geffen signs Sonic Youth: five albums, $300,000, creative control
years.p: Wikipedia reports the terms of the deal that moved the band to Geffen's DGC label.

years.cap: Goo, cover art by Raymond Pettibon.
years.h: Goo and "Kool Thing" feat. Public Enemy's Chuck D
years.p: Gordon wrote the lead single after interviewing LL Cool J for Spin. Chuck D speaks on the track and appears in the video.
years.xp:
The "Kool Thing" video (June 4, 1990, directed by Tamra Davis) was the band's first for a major label. Gordon wanted to wear a beret and carry an Uzi as a "poseur-leftist"; Geffen vetoed it. The single reached No. 7 on Billboard's modern rock chart.

Gordon also wrote "Tunic (Song for Yaryus)" for the album, about Karen Carpenter.

years.h: Gordon co-produces Hole's debut, Pretty on the Inside
years.p: With Don Fleming of Gumball, she cut it in one week at Music Box Studios in Hollywood: four days recording, three mixing.
years.xp: [[Courtney Love|31d2041c-985d-48f7-b6e2-2a70cdf14853]] had pursued her with a letter and a Hello Kitty barrette. Gordon said Love "was either charming and nice or screaming at her band", but rated her as a singer and front person. The album came out September 17, 1991 on Caroline.

years.h: The Year Punk Broke: Sonic Youth tours Europe with Nirvana
years.p: Filmed on the 1991 tour, the documentary caught Sonic Youth alongside [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], Dinosaur Jr., Babes in Toyland, Gumball and Mudhoney.
years.xp: The film, released in 1992, is named for the year Nirvana's Nevermind arrived.

years.src: Wikipedia: Free Kitten · Stereogum: We've Got
years.h: Kim Gordon starts Kitten with Julia Cafritz
years.p: They renamed it [[Free Kitten|7e623dd5-bf40-4f8b-ba71-8226afc918e2]] after a heavy metal singer's lawyers objected to the original name.
years.xp: Gordon says she and Cafritz started the band inspired by Royal Trux. Yoshimi P-We of the Boredoms later played drums and [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]] of Pavement played bass, and the band played Lollapalooza in 1993. Albums: Nice Ass (1995) and Sentimental Education (1997) on Kill Rock Stars.

years.h: Gordon co-directs The Breeders' "Cannonball" video with Spike Jonze
years.p: Gordon also launched the X-Girl clothing line with Daisy von Furth that year.
years.xp: X-Girl grew out of X-Large, co-founded by the Beastie Boys' Mike D; the first store opened in 1994 and Chloe Sevigny modeled for it. Gordon sold her share in 1999.

years.h: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore have a daughter, Coco
years.p: Coco Hayley Moore was born on July 1, 1994. The family moved to Northampton, Massachusetts in 1999.

years.h: Sonic Youth headlines Lollapalooza with Hole and Pavement
years.p: A band that started without a drummer in a gallery now headlined the touring festival.

years.h: Nearly 30 of Sonic Youth's guitars are stolen from a tour van
years.p: Thieves took the instruments in Orange County, California, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: A Matador farewell, then a split
eras.text: Sonic Youth's last album came out on Matador. Two years later, Gordon and Moore separated and the band ended.

years.h: The Eternal · Matador
years.p: The band's final album, on the label that would later release all of Gordon's solo work.

years.cap: Kim Gordon at the Capitol Hill Block Party, July 25, 2009 in Seattle · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Kim Gordon · Stereogum: We've Got
years.h: Gordon and Moore announce they are separating after 27 years
years.p: The band played its final show on November 14, 2011 in Brazil. Gordon later wrote that Moore had an affair; the divorce was finalized in April 2013.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Gordon's account, given in her memoir and interviews. Asked in 2024 about the final show at Brazil's SWU festival, she said she talked about it in her book and does not think about it much anymore.

eras.title: Body/Head and the book
eras.text: With Sonic Youth over, Gordon started an experimental duo in Northampton, wrote a memoir and moved back to Los Angeles.

years.h: Body/Head tours with no drummer and a wall of effects pedals
years.p: Gordon and guitarist [[Bill Nace|ebdcb683-4aee-4ea7-a9ed-38692ebdf9c5]] formed the duo in Northampton around 2011.
years.xp: The name comes from a book about the films of Catherine Breillat. Early shows projected slowed-down film footage behind two guitars and Gordon's voice.

q: It's almost like a Cassavetes film or something.
years.h: Coming Apart · Matador
years.p: A double album of mostly improvised guitar and vocals, edited down from long sessions.
years.xp: Gordon said they played a lot together, then went through and picked the pieces. She said it is not the same as jamming.

years.cap: Girl in a Band, Dey Street Books. Photo needed.
years.h: Girl in a Band covers childhood, Sonic Youth and the marriage
years.p: Dey Street Books published the memoir; Gordon wrote it without a co-writer.
years.xp: Questlove reviewed it in the New York Times, praising its introspection and real feeling; NME called it a record of 50 years of alternative culture. The Guardian felt it was reductive on the marriage's end.

eras.title: Trap beats at 70
eras.text: Gordon's solo records, made with the producer Justin Raisen, pair her voice with hip-hop rhythms. The second earned her first Grammy nominations.

years.h: No Home Record · Matador
years.p: Her first solo album in a 38-year career. She met producer [[Justin Raisen|88728e3a-1dd6-4db4-a21f-d67d8d3dd5c0]] through an Airbnb rental, which also gave a song its title.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.4; the Guardian's Laura Snapes gave it a perfect score. Wikipedia lists the release as October 11, while Gordon's page says October 13.

q: I picked something really mundane, like a packing list, just to contrast it.
years.h: "Bye Bye" opens with a packing list over an 808
years.p: Gordon read an everyday packing list for contrast over a beat [[Justin Raisen|88728e3a-1dd6-4db4-a21f-d67d8d3dd5c0]] made for trap; Stereogum says it was originally made for Playboi Carti. Her daughter Coco is in the video.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Collective · Year-End Lists · ABC · Paste
years.h: The Collective · Matador
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 (reviewer Shaad D'Souza) and ranked it No. 10 of 2024. Metacritic scored it 84.
years.xp:
Gordon said Raisen sent beats and she decided which she could do something on, then added guitar and made up vocals. She told the ABC she works off rhythm better than melody. The title comes from the collective consciousness in Jennifer Egan's novel The Candy House, and Rachel Kushner supplied phrases for lyrics.

The album got two Grammy nominations (Best Alternative Music Album and, for "Bye Bye", Best Alternative Music Performance), her first.

years.h: Gordon plays "Bye Bye" at Glastonbury
years.p: She took the trap-beat songs to the festival stage.

years.h: "BYE BYE 25!" rewrites the song for the Trump administration
years.p: A new version of the single with updated lyrics, released mid-2025.

years.h: Play Me · Matador
years.p: Third solo album, again produced by Raisen. [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] drums on "Busy Bee", which samples Gordon and [[Julia Cafritz|b99fc6af-0753-4f0a-832f-615d9e61394c]] on a 1990s MTV beach house.
